text:
alex: ops-bot alerted p95 timeouts and an uptick in 502/504s for /v1/generate across hosted region eu-west around 09:12 UTC. opening war room.
ops-bot: alert: route=/v1/generate increased 5xx rate 09:11-09:20 UTC (p95 latency up 3x, error-rate +12%). related alerts: auth-service throttle, billing-proxy 429s.
maya: joining — seeing auth cache miss storms (TTL expirations) followed by many calls into billing-check. logs show immediate 429s from billing-proxy then retries bubble into gateway 502s.
jamal: i'm seeing a tight correlation between billing-proxy 429s and KMS latency spikes. sample log line: `2026-03-18T09:13:21Z auth_status=429 billing_check=throttle kms_latency_ms=1200 route=/v1/generate user=acct-987`
sophia: quick mitigation I can roll a patch to bypass non-critical billing checks for existing tokens (skip deep usage validation) and fall back to cached verification. can flip on for EU hosts only. will push to two canary hosts now.
alex: do it. also please add circuit-breaker at gateway so 429s don't cascade into full 5xx wave.
nate: i can reproduce locally with a script that simulates 50 concurrent large-seq requests and forces billing-check for each. repro steps here: 
```
# repro script (quick)
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST https://hosted.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"<very long prompt>"}' &
done
wait
```
This immediately bubbles billing-checks and triggers 429s when billing-proxy connection pool saturates.
oliver: canary patch deployed to eu-canary-1/2 at 09:18. latency down on those hosts already. holding for 10m to confirm.
maya: confirming: after canary flip auth cache miss rate drops 60% on patched hosts; global p95 for /v1/generate down ~35% on canary traffic. looks promising.
jamal: long term root cause hypothesis: billing-proxy added a new per-request validation in last deploy which bypassed the local auth cache on some token paths. when cache TTL aligned across many tokens we saw simultaneous invalidations -> thundering billing-checks -> billing-proxy rate-limit -> auth retries -> gateway 5xx.
kirti: heads-up — support team already triaged high-impact customers. sending a short note to affected accounts with current mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. support-bot: draft msg: "We're investigating increased timeouts and transient 5xxs affecting inference. We've activated a temporary fallback to reduce validation load; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
alex: good. jamal, can you validate deploy diff that added the extra validation? include PR and commit IDs.
jamal: PR #4321 introduced `billing.validate_usage_per_request()` — commit `c7a9f2`. I have a local revert ready. recommend revert + patch that re-enables cache for known token paths.
nate: also saw traffic pattern from 2 customers doing bulk synchronous calls — they account for ~40% of spike. ops: please throttle large single-tenant bursts by default (burst-policy quick fix).
oliver: rolling revert to the validation change on eu region now (09:28). will route traffic gradually off patched hosts with the old behavior until verified.
maya: taking the follow-ups: instrument auth cache metrics (miss, evict, hit) and add alert if miss-rate > 10% in 5m. also adding histogram for billing-proxy 429->retry chains.
jamal: i'll own a postmortem section for the billing-proxy change + testing gaps. will include better load tests and token-warmup guidance.
sophia: action item: add a canary gate in billing-proxy deploys to detect sudden increases in call-rate per-token. assigned to oliver.
kirti: customer comms: send initial update now, then a detailed follow-up when postmortem ready. i'll coordinate with support.
alex: summary of immediate action items:
- maya: auth cache metrics + alert (due EOD)
- jamal: postmortem writeup + revert rationale (tomorrow)
- oliver: canary gate + deploy rollback verification (next 24h)
- sophia: add fallback toggle + config to avoid per-request billing for cached tokens (in progress)
- kirti: customer comms & support FAQ (in progress)
Please add any missing owners or deadlines. we should also add an infra ticket to review KMS call patterns with security (possible key rotation interaction).
support-bot: suggested public status: "Investigating — temporary mitigation in place. No data loss, some requests may still experience transient errors. Engineers are working on a permanent fix."
alex: tagging postmortem follow-up: create incident-** ticket and link to this thread. good work everyone. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: incident closed at 09:45 UTC after rollback and canary verification. generating incident artifacts and logs to attach to the postmortem ticket.
jamal: final note — we need a runbook entry: if billing-proxy 429s spike, immediately enable fallback-token mode and scale billing-proxy pool. i'll draft runbook.
maya: agreed. i'll add playbook steps for cache warmup and TTL staggering.
kirti: i'll wait for the postmortem before sending the detailed customer timeline.
alex: ok closing thread; transferring to postmortem doc and action tracker.
